id_mccall_area.blurb: McCall Area is in west Idaho, around the town of McCall and Payette Lake. Sport leads, followed by bouldering and trad, with a few top ropes. Routes are mostly 5.8 to 5.11, and the boulder problems run from V0 to V8. The Thinking Spot holds the most climbs, nearly all sport, with HIPS Wall and Ping Creek Wall adding more sport routes. Boulders are found around Payette Lake and Jughandle, where Jug Handle Bouldering and the Payette Lake Boulder Circuit are located. Storm Dome and Slick Rock add trad. The best climbing season runs from May to late September.

nm_pond_the.blurb: The Pond is a bouldering area at Ponderosa in the Jemez Mountains of northern New Mexico, beside an irrigation pond. All but one climb is a boulder problem, from V0 to V12, with a broad middle and a solid group of V8 and harder. Most boulders lie west of the pond up a gentle ridge on a good trail, while The Cube is further north up the wash. Ponderosa as a whole is volcanic tuff, sharp and coarse, with thin patina that gives pocketed faces, and it is very exposed to sun and weather. The lower slopes at The Pond can get extremely muddy after snowmelt. Upper Deck holds the most climbs, followed by NASCAR Boulder and Warm-up Boulder.

wv_kaymoor.blurb: Kaymoor is a group of crags on the rim of the New River Gorge near Fayetteville, West Virginia, with walls that face north across from Diamond Point. Sport dominates, with a solid share of trad. Routes are mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with a good number of 5.13s and only a few below 5.10. The climbing is steep, with big holds, and the walls stay shady, which makes it a summer favorite, though they stay wet for at least a day after rain. Butcher's Branch, Rico Suave Buttress, White Wall and Seven Eleven Wall hold the most climbs, and The Hole has the shortest approach of the Kaymoor crags.

ca_highway_18_crags.blurb: The Highway 18 Crags lie along the south side of Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains, most of them near the dam at the lake's western end. Trad leads, followed by sport, with some boulders and top ropes. Grades run from easy to 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 the most common. Castle Rock Area holds the most climbs, followed by Fisherman's Buttress Area and Icebox Canyon. Castle Rock is granite with a relatively shady setting, and snow can linger on the way up into April or May. Fisherman's Buttress is short and technical, with crimpy moves, and the bulk of its better routes are 5.11 and up.

ca_potter_s_point_2.blurb: Potter's Point is a hilltop boulder field in the hills above Santa Barbara on California's Central Coast. Bouldering is nearly everything, with a few bolted sport routes and two top ropes. Problems run from V0 into the V11 range, with a good spread across the moderate grades. The stone is coarse and abrasive, and quality varies: some of it is loose, but a good amount is solid. Expect overhanging and vertical problems with edges and sloping top-outs. The site is exposed with little shade and strong summer sun, so spring and fall are the best seasons. Alcove Area, Main Saddle, Morning Glory and Jacked and Tan hold the most climbs.

co_dark_side_the_5.blurb: The Dark Side is a hillside of boulders at Morrison, Colorado, across the road from the standard Morrison bouldering area. Every climb is a boulder problem, from V0 to V10, with most falling in the V1 to V4 range and a smaller group of harder problems. Shady lines for summer bouldering are plentiful. The hillside is split into many small sub-areas, with Warm-up Traverse Area holding the most climbs, followed by Squirming Coil Area, Arrowhead Arete Area and Dasani Area. The Caves is a cluster of its own. Rattlesnakes are known to frequent the area.
